prompt: In the Cobra version of `hits`, `newTopCmd` declares `var n int` inside the function instead of at package level. What does that buy?
hint: Think of a test that runs the command twice.

choices.text: Every tree `run` builds starts with `-n` at its default of 3
choices.why: Right. A package-level variable keeps the value of the last parse, so a second run without `-n` would still see the first run's number.

choices.text: Cobra refuses to bind a flag to a package-level variable
choices.why: It accepts any pointer; the generator's own template binds flags to package-level variables.

choices.text: The binary is smaller
choices.why: Where a variable is declared makes no difference worth measuring to the binary; the 1,076,140 extra bytes are Cobra, pflag and `text/template`.

choices.text: `-n` becomes visible to `count` as well, as an inherited flag
choices.why: Reach is decided by `Flags()` against `PersistentFlags()`, not by where the variable lives. `count -n 2` is still refused.

prompt: Lesson 1's standard-library `hits` was 4,031,903 bytes and the Cobra build is 5,108,043 bytes. By what percentage did the binary grow, to the nearest whole number?
`go list -m all` printed eight modules, while `go version -m hits` showed only Cobra and pflag as dependencies. What explains the difference?
hint: One command describes the module graph, the other reads the binary.

choices.text: The other modules failed to download and were skipped
choices.why: A module that failed to download would stop the build with an error. These were resolved and simply not imported.

choices.text: The graph includes what Cobra's dependencies need for their own tools and tests; only imported packages get linked
choices.why: Right. `go-md2man`, `blackfriday`, `yaml` and `check.v1` serve Cobra's `doc` package and `yaml`'s tests, and `hits` imports neither.

choices.text: The linker strips modules smaller than a threshold
choices.why: No such threshold exists; a package is linked because something imports it, whatever its size.

choices.text: `go version -m` lists direct dependencies only
choices.why: pflag is an indirect dependency, marked `// indirect` in `go.mod`, and it is listed. The list is what was compiled in.

prompt: Inside a command's `RunE`, the table is written to `cmd.___()`, so that it lands in whatever writer `run` passed to `SetOut`, a test's buffer included.
hint: The method name says it falls back to standard output.

prompt: `./hits top -json access.log` fails with `unknown shorthand flag: 'j' in -json`. Why?
hint: How many letters may follow a single dash in pflag?

choices.text: pflag reads one dash as a run of one-letter shorthands, and there is no `-j`
choices.why: Right. `-json` is read like `ls -la`: `-j -s -o -n`. A long name takes two dashes, `--json`.

choices.text: `--json` is declared on the root, so `top` cannot see it
choices.why: It is persistent, so `top` sees it: `./hits top --number=2 access.log --json` printed JSON.

choices.text: Flags must come after the file name in pflag
choices.why: pflag accepts them on either side; the word `-json` itself is the problem.

choices.text: Boolean flags need an explicit value
choices.why: `--json` with no value set it to true in every transcript.

prompt: Match each command with what the Cobra `hits` did with it.
hint: One of them names a flag on the wrong command.

pairs.right: the status counts as one JSON object
a JSON array of two paths

right_distractors: `access.log` read as the value of `-n`, status 2

prompt: You add a `--since` flag that both `count` and `top` should honour. Where does it go?
hint: Lesson 1 would have declared it twice.

choices.text: In each subcommand's `Flags()`, once per command
choices.why: That works and repeats it, which is lesson 1's arrangement; a third subcommand would need a third copy.

choices.text: On the root, with `PersistentFlags()`
choices.why: Right. Declared once, it reaches every command below the root and is listed under `Global Flags` in their help, like `--json`.

choices.text: On the root, with `Flags()`, since the root runs first
choices.why: `Flags()` is local: a root-only flag would be refused by `count` and `top` as unknown.

choices.text: In `ValidArgsFunction`, which handles everything after the subcommand
choices.why: That function answers Tab for positional arguments; it declares no flags.

prompt: A colleague adds `cmd.Flags().SetInterspersed(false)` to `top`. What does `./hits top access.log -n 2` do now?
hint: Where does pflag stop reading flags once interspersing is off, and what does `top` accept as arguments?

choices.text: It prints the same two-row table as before
choices.why: That needs `-n 2` read as a flag, which interspersing is what allowed after a file name.

choices.text: It shows the default three paths and ignores `-n 2`
choices.why: Nothing is ignored: the words become arguments, and `top` takes one at most.

choices.text: It fails with `accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 3` and status 2
choices.why: Right. Parsing stops at `access.log`, as in lesson 1, so `-n` and `2` become arguments and `MaximumNArgs(1)` refuses three.

choices.text: It tries to open a file called `-n` and exits 1
choices.why: The argument count is checked before `RunE` runs, so no file is opened.

prompt: Who chooses the exit status of the Cobra `hits` when something goes wrong?

choices.text: Cobra, which exits 2 by itself on any usage error
choices.why: Cobra never calls `os.Exit` here; it returns the error and the command it reached.

choices.text: pflag, as the standard library's `flag` did
choices.why: Lesson 1 used `ContinueOnError` to stop `flag` exiting; pflag under Cobra also returns its error.

choices.text: `run`, from the error `ExecuteC` returns
choices.why: Right. `run` prints the error and returns 1 for a `runError`, 2 for anything else; `main` passes that to `os.Exit`.

choices.text: The shell, which maps any error message to status 1
choices.why: The shell only reports the status the process exited with.

prompt: Which of these errors reach `run` WITHOUT the `runError` wrapper, and so end in status 2? Choose all that apply.
hint: Ask which ones happen before any `RunE` starts.

choices.text: `unknown command "cont" for "hits"`
choices.why: Yes. Cobra found no such command while walking the tree, before any `RunE`.

choices.text: `invalid argument "five" for "-n, --number" flag`
choices.why: Yes. pflag refused the value while parsing flags.

choices.text: `accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2`
choices.why: Yes. `cobra.MaximumNArgs(1)` checked the arguments before `RunE`.

choices.text: `open nope.log: no such file or directory`
choices.why: No. `summarise` wraps it in `runError`: the command line was right and the run failed, so it is 1.

choices.text: `line 1: want 5 fields, got 1`
choices.why: No. A line that will not parse is a failed run, wrapped by `summarise`, and ends in 1.

prompt: Somebody deletes `SilenceUsage: true` from the root and keeps everything else. What does `./hits top -n five access.log > out.txt` leave in `out.txt`?
hint: Which writer does Cobra print the usage listing to?

choices.text: Nothing: the usage listing goes to standard error, like the message
choices.why: Cobra prints the usage with `Println`, which uses the writer given to `SetOut` when there is one, and `run` gives it standard output.

choices.text: `top`'s ten-line usage listing, though nothing was counted
choices.why: Right. The message and the hint still go to standard error, but the listing follows `SetOut` into the file meant for results.

choices.text: The table of three paths, because the bad value falls back to the default
choices.why: A value that does not parse is refused; nothing is counted.

choices.text: `Error: invalid argument` followed by the usage
choices.why: `SilenceErrors` is still set, so Cobra prints no `Error:` line anywhere; `run` prints the message to standard error.

prompt: `Args: cobra.___(1)` on `top` is what produced `accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2` when two files were named.
hint: A function from Cobra's family of positional-argument validators, named for an upper bound.

prompt: Why does the root command of `hits` have a `RunE` that only returns an error?
hint: What does Cobra do with a root that has subcommands and nothing to run?

choices.text: Without it Cobra would not add `help` and `completion`
choices.why: Those are added to any root with subcommands, runnable or not.

choices.text: So that a bare `./hits` is a usage mistake with status 2
choices.why: Right. A root with no `RunE` prints its help and returns `nil`, so `./hits` alone would exit 0; the price is a `hits [flags]` line in the help.

choices.text: Cobra panics when a root has no function to run
choices.why: It does not panic; it treats the root as help-only and prints the help.

choices.text: It is how the `Did you mean this?` suggestion is switched on
choices.why: Suggestions come from the unknown-command check while walking the tree, with or without a root `RunE`.

prompt: When Ana presses Tab after `./hits t`, where does the word `top` come from?
hint: The script line 26 printed shows what runs on each Tab.

choices.text: From a list of commands written into the bash script when it was generated
choices.why: The script holds no command names; it runs the program and asks.

choices.text: From `./hits __complete t`, which the script runs and reads
choices.why: Right. The hidden command walks the same tree `hits` runs from and prints `top` and the directive on standard output.

choices.text: From bash, which reads the Go source to find subcommand names
choices.why: bash never sees the source; it only runs the binary it is completing.

choices.text: From the `hits --help` output, which the script parses
choices.why: The script calls `__complete`, whose output is made for it: one candidate per line and a `:4` directive.

prompt: `./hits __complete top ""` ended with a directive line. What number did it carry?
hint: The directive that turns the candidates into file extensions.

prompt: `logFiles` returns `nil, cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp` once a file is already named. What would Tab do without that check?
hint: What would the function return on every call?

choices.text: Offer `.log` files again, for an argument `top` would refuse
choices.why: Right. It would return `log` with directive 8 every time, and a second file would fail `MaximumNArgs(1)` with status 2.

choices.text: Offer nothing, since Cobra already knows the command takes one file
choices.why: Cobra calls the function and passes its answer on; it does not read `Args` for completion.

choices.text: Crash the shell with an error from the script
choices.why: Directive 8 with `log` is a valid answer; the script would filter files as usual.

choices.text: Offer every file in the directory, `notes.txt` included
choices.why: The filter still applies, so only `.log` files and directories would be offered.

prompt: Next month `hits` gains a third subcommand, `slow`. Users saved the bash script months ago. What do they need to do for Tab to offer `slow`?
hint: What does the saved script contain, and what does it ask?

choices.text: Regenerate the script with `hits completion bash` and save it again
choices.why: The script contains no command names, only the call to `__complete`, so the old one asks the new binary.

choices.text: Install the new binary; the old script asks it
choices.why: Right. Every Tab runs `hits __complete`, which reads the tree of whatever binary is installed.

choices.text: Add `slow` to `ValidArgs` on the root
choices.why: Subcommands are completed from the tree; `ValidArgs` is for a fixed list of positional arguments.

choices.text: Install the `bash-completion` package again
choices.why: The package is the script's dependency and does not change with `hits`.

prompt: Put in order what happens when Ana types `./hits t` and presses Tab once.
hint: From the key to the word on the screen.
items: bash calls `__start_hits`, the function registered for `hits`
Cobra walks the tree and finds the commands whose names start with `t`
`hits` prints `top`, its description and `:4` on standard output
bash writes `top` on the command line

prompt: A nightly script written for lesson 1 runs `hits count -json "$f" > counts.json` under `set -e`. The Cobra `hits` is installed in its place. What happens?
hint: Follow the flag, then the exit status.

choices.text: `counts.json` gets the counts, since `-json` is still accepted
choices.why: pflag reads `-json` as shorthands and refuses `-j`; only `--json` works now.

choices.text: `counts.json` gets the table instead of JSON
choices.why: An unknown flag stops the command before `RunE`; nothing is counted.

choices.text: The file stays empty, the message goes to standard error, and status 2 halts everything
choices.why: Right. `unknown shorthand flag: 'j' in -json` and the hint go to standard error, and `set -e` stops at the 2.

choices.text: The script stops with status 1, because a file was involved
choices.why: No file was opened; a refused flag is a mistake in the command line and ends in 2.
